steps: Define user flows (sign‑up/login → habit list → habit detail → insights dashboard). Sketch low‑fidelity wireframes (Figma/pen‑and‑paper – no need for a link).
Set up React project with Vite (fast dev server) or Create‑React‑App.
Install a UI component library (e.g., Radix UI or MUI) for consistent styling.
Build core pages as functional components: AuthPage (login/register), HabitsPage (list + add habit), HabitDetail (daily check‑off), InsightsPage (charts).
Add state‑management (React Context + useReducer or Redux Toolkit if you anticipate complex flows).
Integrate React Router for navigation and protect routes with a simple auth guard.
Set up form validation with React Hook Form + Yup.
Wire up API client using Axios (or native fetch) – keep calls abstracted in a services/ folder.
Write component‑level unit tests with Jest + React Testing Library.
phases.milestone: Live UI prototype hosted on a temporary URL (e.g., Vercel preview) that demonstrates: User registration & login UI (no real backend yet) and ability to create, edit, and delete a habit locally (state persisted in localStorage).

steps: Initialize a Node.js project (npm init) and install Express.
Set up TypeScript (optional but recommended for safety).
Implement authentication: Password hashing with bcrypt; JWT issuance (jsonwebtoken) for stateless auth.

Define RESTful routes: POST /api/auth/register & POST /api/auth/login; GET /api/habits (user‑scoped); POST /api/habits (create); PATCH /api/habits/:id (update status); GET /api/insights (aggregated progress).
Create middleware for request validation (express-validator) and JWT verification (protect habit/insights routes).
Write unit/integration tests with Jest + Supertest.
Add CORS config to allow the React front‑end to call the API.
phases.milestone: Fully functional API server running locally (or on a cloud sandbox) that can: Register / login users, issuing JWTs; Persist habit CRUD operations (stubbed with an in‑memory store for now); Return a JSON payload for the insights endpoint (e.g., “7‑day streak”).

steps: Provision PostgreSQL (local Docker container or managed dev instance).
Design relational schema for users, habits, habit_entries, and insights (materialized view).
Use Prisma ORM (or knex) to generate type‑safe models and migrations.
Replace the in‑memory store in the Express layer with real DB calls (prisma.habit.findMany, etc.).
Implement transactional logic for marking a habit as completed (ensure one entry per day).
Write SQL queries / Prisma aggregations for the insights endpoint: current streak, longest streak, weekly completion rate, heat‑map data.
Add integration tests that spin up a temporary PostgreSQL container (via testcontainers).
Set up database seeding for local development (sample users & habits).
phases.milestone: Production‑grade API connected to a PostgreSQL database, exposing: Secure CRUD for habits; Real‑time insights data (validated against the DB); All tests passing (npm test exits with 0).

steps: Dockerise both services: Dockerfile for React (multi‑stage build → Nginx); Dockerfile for Express (Node base, copy compiled TS, npm start); docker-compose.yml tying together frontend, backend, postgres.
Create environment variable conventions (.env.example) for DB URL, JWT secret, etc.
Set up a CI pipeline (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or CircleCI): Lint → Test → Build Docker images → Push to registry; Deploy to a cloud platform (Render, Railway, Fly.io, or AWS Elastic Beanstalk).
Enable HTTPS (let the platform provide TLS, or use an Nginx reverse‑proxy with Let’s Encrypt).
Configure logging & monitoring (e.g., pino for Node logs, Sentry for error tracking).
(Optional) Turn the React build into a Progressive Web App: add service worker, manifest, offline fallback.
Write end‑to‑end tests with Cypress that run against the deployed staging URL.
phases.milestone: Live production instance reachable at a custom domain, with: Secure user authentication; Persistent habit data & analytics; Automated build‑test‑deploy pipeline.
